nutshell: Chicago is America's Irish-session capital and its biggest folk institution town. About 89 public Irish sessions a month run in roughly 30 pubs, from Lincoln Park to Oak Lawn and the McHenry County exurbs. They are led by a near-professional core (Jimmy Keane, John Williams, Pauline Conneely, Larry Nugent) with a lineage back to police chief Francis O'Neill's 1900s tune-collecting network and the 1956 Irish Musicians Association. The Old Town School of Folk Music (1957) taught 33,845 students in 2025 on a $17.6M budget, and it still runs free half-hour singalongs. Around these sit a weekly Monday contra in the Irish American Heritage Center's ballroom, four Sacred Harp singings, 50-year-old suburban sing-arounds in brewpubs and church basements, and a deep heritage layer: 16 NEA Heritage Fellows in the metro, sold-out bomba schools, górale fiddlers, a 73rd-year urban powwow, tamburitza and blues jams. Old-time is the thin spot: there is one weekly open jam, in a pizza parlour.

venues.name: FitzGerald's Nightclub

Known for Louisiana and Texas roots music (credited with bringing Clifton Chenier and zydeco to Chicago audiences) and the July 4th-weekend American Music Festival (43rd in 2026). Building was a 1911 dance hall and, as Club Ritz, a Capone-gang hangout.

organizations.notes: Building opened 1985/86 in Mayfair; 2,500-4,000 attend its St. Patrick's celebration.

organizations.name: Chicago Gaelic Park
organizations.notes: Land bought 1983, opened 1985, Oak Forest; 53 acres; The Carraig pub.

organizations.name: Irish Musicians Association of America
organizations.notes: Founded by Chicago immigrants including Kevin Henry in the 1950s (1956 per a secondary summary); held an annual concert recorded by the LoC in 1977.

organizations.name: Irish Music School of Chicago
organizations.notes: Founded by Seán Cleland; teaches by ear.

organizations.name: Chicago Scots
organizations.notes: 'Oldest not-for-profit organization in Illinois'; runs the Highland Games and Caledonia Senior Living.

organizations.name: Chicago Spelmanslag
organizations.notes: Led by Mary Allsopp; Swedish and Norwegian repertoire; heard at Folk & Roots and Square Roots.

organizations.name: Old Town Teachers Organization (OTTO), Illinois Federation of Teachers
organizations.notes: Faculty voted to unionize on Jan 16, 2019, in the middle of the Armitage-sale fight. Bargaining began October 2019, with federal mediation from March 2021. The first contract (including a 4% raise and wider health-insurance eligibility) was reached in early June 2022 after a nine-hour session (Block Club, Sun-Times, Axios). The school's FAQ describes 'over 200 part-time teachers' in the unit.

organizations.name: Save Old Town School
organizations.kind: student, faculty and alumni advocacy group
organizations.notes: Formed in fall 2018 to fight the sale of 909 W Armitage; petitions, letters and rallies led the board to postpone and then, in March 2019, drop the sale. Spokesman Rich Gordon: 'Rather than sell the building they should fix the problems.'

organizations.name: Fox Valley Folklore Society (FVFS)
organizations.notes: Batavia-based society (P.O. Box 1088). Runs the Fox Valley Folk Music & Storytelling Festival (Labor Day, Geneva; 49th in 2025), a weekly Wednesday sing-around (since 1975), a Monday Zoom sing, a monthly sea shanty sing, monthly old-time barn dances in Glen Ellyn, and a storytelling guild. Co-founder Juel Ulven was inducted posthumously into the Fox Valley Arts Hall of Fame in March 2026; board in 2026: Heidi Knuth, Ursa Miles, Phil Cooper, Cheryl Joyal, Lynn Garren, Jessi Laffey. Exact founding year not found; activity dates to at least 1975.

organizations.name: Plank Road Folk Music Society (PRFMS)
organizations.notes: Western-suburbs club (P.O. Box 176, Downers Grove); dues $20 a year ($30 family); quarterly newsletter QuarterNotes; three 'Down the Old Plank Road' albums. Its all-volunteer Plank Road String Band (founded by Cathy Jones, Mark Dvorak, Marianne Mohrhusen and Marvin Lensik) rehearses monthly in Lombard and plays its barn dances. President Bob O'Hanlon.

organizations.name: Lake County Folk Club
organizations.notes: Grayslake-based. Monthly concert, open stage and song circle, plus virtual song shares. Past president Chuck VanderVennet has long hosted the Woodstock Folk Festival.

organizations.name: Two Way Street Coffee House
organizations.kind: church-based coffeehouse ministry (First Congregational UCC, Downers Grove)
organizations.notes: Began as a drop-in center for local teens; Friday concerts; recorded concerts for Downers Grove cable from 1982; flooded April 2013 and reopened the same year after renovation. New since 2025: 5th Saturdays workshops, a Heritage Matinee Series (raised over $2,000) and Cultural Connections (Nordic jams and dances with Chicago Spelmanslag). 'Tunes and Tales' songwriter rounds planned for 2026.

organizations.name: Chicago Sacred Harp Singers / Sacred Harp Singing in Chicago (incl. University of Chicago Shapenote Singing Association)
organizations.notes: Founded in the early 1980s by Ted and Marcia Johnson, Judy Hauff and others, arriving through the folk revival rather than church choirs. Co-organized the first Illinois State Sacred Harp Convention (Paxton, May 25, 1985) with Hugh McGraw. Today: four regular local singings (Hyde Park, North Side, Logan Square, Fox Valley) and five or six annual singings. Email list hosted at lists.uchicago.edu.

organizations.name: Chicago Shanties
organizations.notes: groups.io list (282 members, 957 topics); monthly sing at the Old Town School; contact Kathy Whisler; maritime performers Tom Kastle, David Yondorf and John Wohlers are listed with it.

organizations.name: Chicago Maritime Museum (formerly Chicago Maritime Society)
organizations.notes: At 1200 W 35th St (Bridgeport) since about 2016; 2026 events include an Oct 29 fundraising 'Chicago Maritime Museum Festival' with sea shanties ($100) and a Lee Murdock Great Lakes Christmas concert.

organizations.name: Woodstock Folk Festival (organization)
organizations.notes: Founded by Amy Beth and Melodee Ladd. Gives a Lifetime Achievement Award (Art Thieme 2002, Ella Jenkins 2003, Bonnie Koloc 2010, Tom Paxton 2012, Corky Siegel 2018, Magpie 2026) and, since 2018, 'Woody' Awards. Also runs spring benefit concerts.

organizations.name: Acoustic Renaissance Concerts
organizations.notes: Hinsdale; about 31 seasons.

organizations.name: SPACE Presents
organizations.notes: SPACE's promotion arm; produces the Evanston Folk Festival (2024-).

organizations.name: National Convention of Gospel Choirs and Choruses
organizations.notes: Co-founded in Chicago by Thomas A. Dorsey to train gospel singers and musicians nationwide; its current Chicago activity was not researched here.

organizations.name: Chicago School of Violin Making
organizations.notes: Founded by Kenneth Warren & Son as the Kenneth Warren & Son School of Violin Making.

organizations.name: Chicago Barn Dance Company (CBDC)
organizations.kind: contra & traditional square dance society (CDSS affiliate listing)
organizations.notes: Runs the weekly Monday dance at the IAHC and keeps the regional dance calendar, which covers IL, NW Indiana and Wisconsin. Members sign up at dances in Feb-Mar; board term May 2025-Apr 2027 (president Devin Pohly). A 2010 video shows the Monday dance at Bethany Church Hall on Paulina. 93 dancers on 30 Dec 2024 (CBDC Facebook). Founding year not found.

organizations.name: Queer Contra Chicago
organizations.notes: Relaunched 2017 after an earlier incarnation; about 50-60 dancers a month in 2019. Organizers include Moose Flores (since 2017), Andrea Craft and Qwill Duvall; Inigo Santiago joined in early 2026.

organizations.name: UChicago Folk Arts Community / UChicago Folklore Society
organizations.notes: The Folk Arts Community runs the monthly contra. The Folklore Society runs the University of Chicago Folk Festival (66th edition Feb 2026, so first held in 1961). Founding year given is the festival's.

organizations.name: Valparaiso Oldtime Dance Society
organizations.notes: Nonprofit; "American, Celtic and English traditional dance, music and song".

organizations.name: Plank Road Folk Music Society
organizations.notes: "Since 1985"; 40th-anniversary party June 2025. Runs barn dances, the string band, sing-arounds and a song circle with Two Way Street Coffee House. Publishes the QuarterNotes newsletter.

organizations.name: Chicagoland English Country Dancers & IFD
organizations.kind: English country & international folk dance (CDSS affiliate)
organizations.notes: Founded Jan 2006 by Mady Newfield & Tammy Bretscher; caller Cheryl Yenter (North). Runs the Harvest Moon Dance Weekend (St. Charles). Fragrance-free policy.

organizations.name: Evanston Monday Night Folk Dancers
organizations.notes: Hybrid in-person/Zoom.

organizations.name: Ethnic Dance Chicago (EDC)
organizations.notes: Midwest regional dance calendar; ran 12-week "Inside Balkan Dance" courses (2019); runs the "Virtual Dance Room".

organizations.name: Chicago Folk Dance Council
organizations.notes: Kept a "Folk Dance Scene" listing hosted at fnal.gov, last updated 2019.

organizations.name: Ensemble Balkanske Igre
organizations.notes: Thursday open class; co-organises the Spring Festival of Balkan music & dance (billed "60th anniversary" on its current page).

organizations.name: Chicago Israeli Folk Dancing
organizations.notes: Chicago's longest-running recreational Israeli folk dance session. Connected to the Machol Merkaz Midwest Israeli dance camp.

organizations.name: RSCDS Chicago Branch
organizations.notes: Class began 7 Feb 1980 in Palos Park; branch status 1987 (teachers Martin Mulligan, David & Avril Quarrie). Demo team at the Highland Games; Midwinter Ball; co-hosts the Midwest Scottish Weekend with Milwaukee & Madison.

organizations.name: Chicagoland Scottish Fiddle and Accordion Club (CSFAC)
organizations.notes: Monthly meetings at Seman Violins, Skokie (Jan & Jul 2026 listed).

organizations.name: Francis O'Neill Club
organizations.notes: Weekly céilí and set dancing at the IAHC; Céilí Mór with the band Ceoltóirí Chicago; Alan Beale Workshop Weekend (Oct).

organizations.name: Irish Musicians Association of America (IMA) / Comhaltas
organizations.notes: Founded 19 Aug 1956 at the Midland Hotel, Chicago, with musicians from eight US cities; Illinois charter 1958 (signatories Frank Thornton, Kevin Henry, Johnny McGreevy, Jimmy Neary, Jimmy Donnelly). Its Session-member president calls it "the oldest Comhaltas branch in the United States". Covers NE Illinois, NW Indiana and SE Wisconsin; based at the IAHC. The Comhaltas North American Convention was held at the Northbrook Hilton, 9-13 Apr 2026.

organizations.name: West Suburban Irish
organizations.notes: Naperville; sponsors the monthly Quigley's session.

organizations.name: Northern Illinois Bluegrass Association (NIBA)
organizations.notes: Keeps a public Google jam calendar (bluegrassassociation@gmail.com) and a 16-page monthly members' newsletter.

organizations.name: Bluegrass Chicago
organizations.notes: Timely calendar with 149 bluegrass-related entries in 2026, mostly performances; the most current source for jams.

organizations.name: Fiddle Club of the World (Chicago Chapter)
organizations.notes: Convened by Paul Tyler in 2008 under the Old Town School; independent since 2013. 44 artist meetings in its first six years with fiddlers from 8 countries. Sponsored the Midwest Fiddle Championship 2009-2015. New Dunelands Chapter (Miller Beach, IN) in 2026.

organizations.name: Pullman Morris and Sword
organizations.notes: Far South Side (Pullman); weekly Sunday practice; hosted the 2015 Midwest Morris Ale.

organizations.name: Ravenswood Morris
organizations.notes: Listed by NAMDO; practice details only from 2001.

organizations.name: Mortarbordis Border Morris
organizations.notes: Danced the Pullman May Day with Pullman Morris and Sword (2023, 2024).

organizations.name: Metropolitan Chicago Association of Square Dancers (MCASD)
organizations.notes: About 17 active clubs on its Oct-Nov 2026 calendar, covering Cook, DuPage, Kane, Lake, McHenry and Will counties plus Hebron, IN. Promotion site UcanSquareDance.com.

organizations.name: Chi-Town Squares
organizations.notes: On the MCASD calendar (Oct & Nov 2026).

organizations.name: Chicago Cajun & Zydeco Music
organizations.notes: Hosts the monthly Chicago Cajun Jam.

festivals.name: Chicago Powwow (American Indian Center)
festivals.notes: 73rd annual on Sat Oct 3 2026 at Schiller Woods-East, Grove 13; grand entries 11am and 3pm; intertribal, invited drums, specials ('competition does not define the powwow'). 2025 (72nd) host drum: Smokeytown. Founding year inferred from numbering.

festivals.name: Powwow at the Lake (AIC)
festivals.notes: First held Thu July 25 2024 at Foster Beach (Park District 'Night Out in the Parks'); 500+ attendees, round dance of 100+. Announced as annual; 2025 and 2026 editions not verified.

festivals.name: Harvest Pow Wow (Midwest SOARRING Foundation)
festivals.notes: Largest SOARRING powwow; first ten years in Mokena, later western suburbs; 2026 edition at DuPage County Fairgrounds cancelled, 2027 planned.

festivals.name: Indigifest (AIC)
festivals.notes: 2025 edition; Indigenous music, dance, food in a city park.

festivals.name: Puerto Rican Fest / Fiestas Patronales Puertorriqueñas and People's Parade
festivals.notes: Site advertises the '45th annual' fest in Humboldt Park (2026) and the '47th annual Puerto Rican People's Day Parade' (June 14 2025, Division & Campbell); bomba, plena, salsa stages. Numbering conflicts with accounts of a 1966 first parade (followed by the Division Street riots); an 800,000 attendance claim appears only in a search summary.

festivals.name: Fiesta Boricua
festivals.notes: On Paseo Boricua between the two steel flags, organized by the Puerto Rican Cultural Center; bomba and plena. Founding year and a '150,000+' crowd figure come from a festival-listing site (low confidence).

festivals.name: Fiesta del Sol
festivals.notes: Pilsen (Cermak & Allport), free; site says '55th annual' (2026) and lists 2027 dates Jul 29-Aug 1, but its FAQ calls 2027 the '54th'. Numbering implies a start around 1972.

festivals.name: UIC Latin American Music Festival / UIC Mariachi Festival
festivals.notes: Oct 9-11 2025; mariachi festival day Oct 9 at Merit School of Music for high school and community mariachis ($100/group), clinics and combined performance.

festivals.name: Taste of Polonia
festivals.notes: Copernicus Center, Jefferson Park; up to ~40,000 (Nadig Newspapers); other accounts give 30,000-60,000 and 1980 as the first official year.

festivals.name: IPA Chicago Festival of Bands (National Polka Month)
festivals.notes: 58th annual Jan 15-17 2027 at Elements by the Odyssey, Orland Park; founding year inferred from numbering. Lenny Gomulka & Chicago Push played the Jan 18 2025 edition.

festivals.name: Festiwal na Góralską Nutę (On the Highlander Tune Festival)
festivals.notes: 43rd edition Nov 7-8 2026 at Dom Podhalan (42nd: Nov 8-9 2025); multi-group górale music and dance showcase. Founding year inferred.

festivals.name: Józefinki Muzykanckie and the Karol Stoch Waka soloists' and musicians' review (ZPPA)
festivals.notes: Annual górale musicians' gathering (Mar 15 2026) and the 6th review of Podhale soloists and bands named for fiddler Karol Stoch 'Waka' (May 3 2026).

festivals.name: Pierogi Fest
festivals.notes: 119th St, downtown Whiting, IN (Lake Co., IN); polka dance contest, Buscias songfest, parade; started as a 50-foot stretch of booths and 1,200 pierogi.

festivals.name: SerbFest
festivals.notes: St. Sava Serbian Orthodox Church, Merrillville, IN; Jul 31-Aug 2 2026; tamburitza and Serbian folk music, historical society exhibit.

festivals.name: Chicago Blues Festival
festivals.notes: Created by Lois Weisberg; free; Grant Park then Millennium Park from 2017; skipped 2020; billed as the largest free festival of its kind.
festivals.place: Grant Park (Petrillo Music Shell) to 2016; Millennium Park since 2017

festivals.name: Chicago Gospel Music Festival
festivals.notes: Jul 24-25 2026, Pritzker Pavilion, free; frames Chicago as birthplace of gospel (Thomas A. Dorsey).

festivals.name: African Festival of the Arts
festivals.notes: 35th annual Aug 30-Sep 1 2025 in Washington Park after a one-year hiatus; 'Drum Village' participatory drum circle. Founding year inferred from numbering (approximate).

festivals.name: Chicago Gaelic Park Irish Fest
festivals.notes: Aug 21-23 2026, Oak Forest.
festivals.place: Chicago Gaelic Park, Oak Forest (Cook County)

festivals.name: Assyrian New Year (Akitu / Kha b-Nisan) parade and celebrations
festivals.notes: Parade on Western Ave from Devon (Apr 6 2025, per search summary), followed by khigga dancing at picnics and parties; low-quality sources.

festivals.name: Skokie Festival of Cultures
festivals.notes: Oakton Park, Skokie, May 17-18 2025; Assyrian dance performance and cultural tent among many communities.

festivals.name: Ensemble Español American Spanish Dance and Music Festival
festivals.notes: Annual festival produced by Ensemble Español at NEIU.

festivals.name: University of Chicago Folk Festival
festivals.place: Mandel Hall and Ida Noyes Hall, Hyde Park, Chicago
festivals.notes: Student-run by the UChicago Folklore Society (formed early 1950s). Held every winter since 1961; 66th annual on Feb 20-21, 2026 with High Fidelity (bluegrass), Gap Civil (old-time), Lissa Schneckenburger & Garrett Cameron (Celtic), Luke Huval Band (Cajun), Jontavious Willis, Ethan Leinwand, Mariachi Flor de Primavera; free Saturday workshops and dances; concerts streamed. 1961 bill: Stanley Brothers, New Lost City Ramblers, Elizabeth Cotten, Roscoe Holcomb, Willie Dixon. Attendance not published.

festivals.name: Fox Valley Folk Music & Storytelling Festival
festivals.place: Wheeler Park (earlier Island Park), Geneva, Kane County
festivals.notes: Run by the Fox Valley Folklore Society with the Geneva Park District. 49th annual Aug 31-Sep 1 2025; 50th annual Sep 6-7 2026. Six stages, ~17 featured performers, jams and sings, folk-dance workshops, Sunday-night barn dance. Suggested donation $35/day ($20 teens/seniors). Founding year inferred from the 49th edition in 2025. FVFS co-founder Juel Ulven inducted posthumously into the Fox Valley Arts Hall of Fame, March 2026.

festivals.name: Square Roots Festival
festivals.place: Lincoln Ave between Montrose and Wilson, Lincoln Square, Chicago
festivals.notes: Street festival co-run by the Old Town School of Folk Music and the Lincoln Square Ravenswood Chamber of Commerce; successor to OTS's Folk & Roots Festival (Welles Park, 1998 to about 2010). 2026 dates July 10-12. Attendance 45,000+ in 2025 per OTS's 2025 filing (CauseIQ). Founding year approximate: DrDosido recordings show Square Roots by 2012; Folk & Roots still listed in 2011 by one source.

festivals.name: Irish American Heritage Center Irish Fest (Irish American Heritage Festival)
festivals.month: summer (dates vary; one 2025 listing gives Sep 13-15)
festivals.notes: IAHC formed 1976 out of the Shamrock American Club (1939), bought the old Mayfair School in 1985 and opened 1986. Founding year of the festival itself is only supported by secondary summaries; dates of the 2025 edition come from an aggregator listing. Treat as low-medium confidence.

festivals.name: Chicago Scots Scottish Festival & Highland Games
festivals.notes: 40th annual June 12-13, 2026 (founding inferred). Friday-night ceilidh with caller and live fiddle band; claims the largest pipe band competition in North America (50+ bands). Run by Chicago Scots, founded 1845, 'the oldest not-for-profit organization in Illinois'.

festivals.name: Frankfort Bluegrass Festival
festivals.place: Breidert Green and Prairie Park, downtown Frankfort (Will County)
festivals.notes: Free, all-volunteer, two days; 12th annual July 13-14, 2024 (so founded 2013) with Peter Rowan, Jim Lauderdale & Po' Ramblin' Boys, AJ Lee & Blue Summit, Special Consensus and Korea's Country GongBang. Former IBMA Event of the Year. Founding committee member Steve Haberichter. Festival site did not load for 2025/2026 confirmation.

festivals.name: FitzGerald's American Music Festival
festivals.notes: Roots/Americana/zydeco/blues; 42nd edition July 3-6, 2025, ~50 acts on three stages. FitzGerald's became the first Illinois nightclub on the National Register of Historic Places (2025). Earl Pionke's 2013 memorial was held here.

festivals.name: Breaking Up Thanksgiving (contra dance weekend)
festivals.notes: Chicago Barn Dance Company weekend: Friday and Saturday contra dances, Saturday workshops, Sunday brunch and waltzing. 2025: Nov 28-30; weekend pass $45 adults. Founding year not found.

festivals.name: Midwest Fleadh Cheoil (Comhaltas Mid-West Region)
festivals.place: rotates; Chicago hosted Apr 25-27, 2025; St. Louis May 8-10, 2026
festivals.notes: The region's Irish music competition, qualifying for the All-Ireland Fleadh. In 1977 the Library of Congress recorded the 'Annual Midwest Fleadh Cheoil' at Bogan High School, 79th & Pulaski. Chicago as 2025 host comes from search summaries only.

festivals.name: Milwaukee Irish Fest
festivals.place: Henry Maier Festival Park, Milwaukee, WI (about 90 miles north)
festivals.notes: Founded by Edward J. Ward; ~250 acts on 17 stages; closes with 'the Scattering', a mass session. Heavily attended by Chicago Irish musicians. Its Ward Irish Music Archives remastered Francis O'Neill's wax cylinders.

festivals.name: Woodstock Folk Festival
festivals.notes: Free, noon to 6pm on the historic Woodstock Square (McHenry County); 41st edition July 19, 2026, main stage hosted by folk DJs Marilyn Rea Beyer (WFMT) and Lilli Kuzma (WDCB); ends with an All-Sing finale.

festivals.name: Evanston Folk Festival
festivals.notes: Produced by SPACE Presents at Dawes Park on the lakefront. 2024 drew 4,500 (Saturday) + 4,000 (Sunday) plus about 500 free kids a day (Chicago Tribune); 2026 headliners included the Indigo Girls, Trampled by Turtles, Josh Ritter, Valerie June and Sierra Hull; 2027 is set for Sep 11-12. Organizers sought permission for three more years (Evanston Now, Jan 2026).

festivals.name: Square Roots Festival (Old Town School + Lincoln Square-Ravenswood Chamber)
festivals.notes: Three-day street festival on Lincoln Avenue run with the Lincoln Square-Ravenswood Chamber of Commerce; 45,000+ attendees in 2025, the most to date; 2026 dates July 10-12; proceeds fund scholarships and residencies. Continues the Folk & Roots Festival held in Welles Park from 1998: Wikipedia counts Square Roots as one festival 'since 1998', and Anvara says it moved onto Lincoln Avenue as Square Roots in 2012. The school's history says Folk & Roots ran 13 years, which would put the switch at 2010-11.

festivals.name: Fretboard Summit
festivals.notes: Guitar and luthier summit co-presented by the Old Town School and Fretboard Journal; 2025: 472 attendees from 29 states and 9 countries, 94 luthiers and vendors, concerts by Lyle Lovett and others.

festivals.name: Chicago Maritime Festival
festivals.notes: Maritime music festival organized by Tom and Chris Kastle, usually at the Chicago History Museum; 'not uncommon for over 500 people to participate'; held 2003-2020 and 2022 onward per Wikipedia. The old festival domain now hosts spam. In 2026 the Chicago Maritime Museum's 'Festival' was an October 29 fundraiser with shanties, so the February music-festival format may have lapsed (unverified).

festivals.name: Midwest Sacred Harp Convention
festivals.notes: Two-day convention; 2026: May 30-31 at the Broadway Armory, 5917 N Broadway, Chicago (chair Erik Schwab). Ted and Marcia Johnson co-chaired it for years. Founding year not found.

festivals.name: Chicago Anniversary Singing (Sacred Harp)
festivals.notes: 2026: Jan 11, with workshops Jan 10; historically held at Kilbourn Park Fieldhouse.

festivals.name: Chicago Ann Sleeva Memorial Singing (Cooper Book)
festivals.notes: 11th annual edition Saturday Aug 8, 2026 at The CheckOut, 4116 N Clark St; sings from the 2012 Cooper revision of The Sacred Harp (founding year computed from the edition count).

festivals.name: Hyde Park All-Day Singing (Sacred Harp and Missouri Harmony)
festivals.notes: Saturday before the first Sunday in November (2025: Nov 1).

festivals.name: Illinois State Sacred Harp Convention
festivals.notes: First held at Paxton, IL, organized by the Chicago and Charleston (Eastern Illinois University) groups with Hugh McGraw and Georgia singers; downstate (Charleston area) since. Its status after 2017 was not checked in detail.

festivals.name: Old Town School Folk & Roots Festival
festivals.notes: Held in Welles Park 'every July for the next 13 years' from 1998; succeeded by Square Roots.

festivals.name: Breaking Up Thanksgiving
festivals.notes: Contra and old-time dance weekend at the IAHC, 27-29 Nov 2026. Historically open band and open caller, once all night; now pre-scheduled slots.

festivals.name: Alan Beale Workshop Weekend (Irish set dancing)
festivals.notes: 2-4 Oct 2026 at the IAHC, with teacher Ultan Mulcahy.

festivals.name: Harvest Moon Dance Weekend (English country dance)
festivals.notes: 3-5 Oct 2026, St. Charles, IL.

festivals.name: Spring Festival of Balkan music & dance
festivals.notes: Billed as the "60th anniversary" festival; long tied to International House at UChicago. Current-year status not confirmed.

festivals.name: June Camp (Midwest international folk dance weekend)
festivals.notes: Chicago-area camp directed by Mady Newfield for nearly 25 years.

festivals.name: Chicago Scottish Festival & Highland Games
festivals.notes: Bills its pipe band competition as the largest in North America (50+ bands); Friday-night ceilidh (12 Jun 2026).

festivals.name: Countryside Bluegrass Festival
festivals.notes: 12 Sep 2026; ends with a jam session.

festivals.name: Midwest Fiddle (& Banjo) Championship at Square Roots
festivals.notes: Started by Paul Tyler at the Old Town School festival (2nd contest 2004); 14th annual in 2016. Not verified for 2024-26, so status is uncertain.

festivals.name: Indiana Fiddle Frolic
festivals.notes: Fiddle Club of the World event (3rd annual 2025) at Ross Camp, Indiana. Outside the MSA.

festivals.name: Comhaltas North American Convention (hosted)
festivals.notes: Rotating convention, held at the Hilton Chicago/Northbrook, 9-13 Apr 2026.

instruction.name: AfriCaribe Music & Dance Academy
instruction.scale: Bomba and plena dance/drum classes for children and adults in four 6-week quarters; 90-minute classes with history; recital each session.

instruction.name: La Escuelita Bombera de Corazón semester classes
instruction.scale: 7 class offerings at $150 (bomba drumming buleo I/II, dance I/II, plena güiro & pandereta, song & history, Bomba Kids); all listed sold out in Oct 2026.

instruction.name: SRBCC paid apprenticeships
instruction.scale: Ages 14-22 learn Afro-Caribbean jazz and percussion from master teaching artists.

instruction.name: Sones de México Mexican Music School / guitar classes 'En Español'
instruction.scale: Guitar classes in Spanish plus school outreach.

instruction.name: Old Town School of Folk Music: son jarocho jarana workshop (Patricio Hidalgo with Son de Madera)
instruction.scale: One-off workshop with jaranas provided, followed by a fandanguito; date not shown.

instruction.name: Orozco Academy mariachi after-school (PCCCA)
instruction.scale: Grades 3-8, Tue/Thu 3:30-5pm, three terms 2025-26, $510/yr.

instruction.name: Chicago Mariachi Project
instruction.scale: In-school and after-school mariachi in many CPS schools plus audition-based youth academy ensembles, ages 8-18 (per search summary; site not reachable).

instruction.name: Mariachi Matters
instruction.scale: Free one-year program, ages 7-12, Romeoville.

instruction.name: Ballet Folklórico de Chicago academy
instruction.scale: 400+ students, open 7 days, ages 2 to seniors.

instruction.name: Muntu Dance Theatre community classes
instruction.scale: Weekly Saturday $15 class, teens and adults.

instruction.name: Cambodian museum music and dance classes
instruction.scale: Pinpeat, Khmer traditional music, Khmer dance; 10-session terms.

instruction.name: KCCoC Chicago Poongmul School
instruction.scale: Korean percussion school in Wheeling.

instruction.name: Junior Klezmer Orchestra
instruction.scale: Grades 5-12, twice monthly; 5-6 public performances a year.

instruction.name: ZPPA Szkółka Pieśni i Tańca (song & dance school) and Mali Siumni
instruction.scale: Children's górale song and dance groups at Dom Podhalan.

instruction.name: Trinity Irish Dance Academy
instruction.scale: Nine locations in IL and WI.

instruction.name: Natya Dance Theatre school
instruction.scale: Bharatanatyam training; 50 years in 2025.

instruction.name: Ensemble Español classes (adult, children, After School Matters)
instruction.scale: Flamenco and Spanish dance; university residency at NEIU.

instruction.name: AIC Drum & Dance
instruction.scale: Free twice-weekly drum, song and powwow dance instruction (2023 page; current status unverified).

instruction.name: Old Town School of Folk Music - group classes, private lessons, workshops
instruction.scale: 2025: 276 teaching artists served 24,542 people in group classes, 5,060 in private lessons and 4,243 in workshops (33,845 total), across 3 Chicago buildings plus 5 suburban Wiggleworms branches. '700+ accredited class offerings'. Eight-week sessions (next began Oct 26, 2026); most group classes have 4-14 students. Group-class registrations by category: guitar 22.3%, Wiggleworms 17.9%, dance 14.7%, ensemble 9.8%, piano 8.6%, voice 8.2%, other adult 7.2%, string band 5.4%, kids music 4.5%, teen 1.3%. Fiddle track: Intro to Violin/Fiddle, then Fiddle 1-4, plus Irish fiddle (Devin Shepherd, Sean Colledge); other fiddle teachers include Maggie Neatherlin, Colby Maddox and Jordan Wankoff. Price: $264 per 80-minute weekly class for 8 weeks ($244 for members), versus $48 for an 8-week session in the mid-1970s. Financial aid of $207,468 went to 397 enrollees in 2025.

instruction.name: Old Town School Old Time String Ensemble
instruction.scale: Taught by Paul Tyler and Steve Rosen since 1990; 20-30 members by the mid-1990s; learns tunes by ear to prepare students for outside jams. Current status not separately verified.

instruction.name: Wiggleworms (Old Town School early-childhood music)
instruction.scale: Started 1985 by Kathy Lahiff; more than 4,000 registrations in 2025; branches in Evanston, Glen Ellyn, Naperville, Park Ridge and Western Springs; 23% of the school's enrollment in 2016.

instruction.name: Old Town School 'Sea Music and Shanty Sing' class
instruction.scale: Catalog class on songs sung in Chicago and on the Great Lakes 'during the heyday of commercial sail'; current scheduling not verified.

instruction.name: Irish Music School of Chicago
instruction.scale: Kids' and adult classes, private lessons, Irish Arts Kids Day Camp, master workshops, Sunday family session; founded by fiddler Seán Cleland; enrollment figures not published.

instruction.name: Academy of Irish Music (founded by Noel Rice)
instruction.scale: Youth Irish music academy led by flute player and historian Noel Rice (died 2019, age 84). Current activity unverified (Facebook page, 894 followers). The Library of Congress holds a 1977 interview with Rice about teaching Irish music and dance in Chicago.

instruction.name: Murphy Roche Irish Music Club / Institute of Traditional Irish Music (Comhaltas branch)
instruction.scale: Comhaltas Ceoltóirí Éireann branch (formerly the Murphy Roche branch) at 11309 72nd St, Burr Ridge; reported as host of a CCE North American convention and immersion weekend in Chicago (date not verified). Scale not published.

instruction.name: Chicago School of Violin Making
instruction.scale: Full-time luthier training founded by Kenneth Warren & Son; not a folk school, but part of the city's instrument-making ecosystem.

instruction.name: Plank Road String Band monthly practices
instruction.scale: Open community string band (intermediate players) rehearsing 2nd Saturdays 2-4pm, Sep-Apr, at First Church of Lombard; plays the Plank Road barn dances; downloadable tune list and melody and chord sheets.

instruction.name: Two Way Street / Plank Road '5th Saturdays' workshop series
instruction.scale: Workshops in months with a fifth Saturday (e.g. Lil' Rev on harmonica and ukulele, May 2026; 'Murder Ballads: From Song to Story' with the Fox Valley Folklore Society, Oct 31 2026, $25). A third year was planned for 2026.

instruction.name: Front Porch Music lessons
instruction.scale: Shop-based lessons and a 'Blues Project'; Valparaiso, IN.

instruction.name: Midwest Banjo Camp
instruction.scale: Annual 4-day old-time and bluegrass banjo camp (June 11-14, 2026) with guitar, fiddle, mandolin and bass tracks; held in Michigan, outside the MSA. Its faculty has included Chicago's Greg Cahill (Special Consensus) and mandolinist Don Stiernberg.

instruction.name: Old Town School of Folk Music (fiddle, Irish ensemble, bodhrán)

instruction.scale: Monthly Sept-Apr

radio.notes: Saturdays 9pm-midnight; 'folk music & farce, show tunes & satire'. Created by Mike Nichols (later the film director); hosted by Norman Pellegrini and Ray Nordstrand, then Rich Warren (co-host from 1983, sole host 1996-2020, 'never missed an episode'). Lead Belly's 'Midnight Special' is the theme. Chicago's longest-running radio program. Rea Beyer, formerly of Boston's WUMB, entered the Folk Alliance Folk DJ Hall of Fame in 2023.

Saturdays 8-9pm; one-hour folk concert; about two dozen live concerts a year from local venues (e.g. Acoustic Renaissance in Hinsdale) or the WFMT studio, plus '45 years' of archive recordings (implying a start around 1980).

radio.station: WDCB 90.9 FM (College of DuPage, Glen Ellyn)
radio.notes: Tuesdays 8-11pm, presented live; traditional and contemporary folk plus folk-rock, bluegrass, Celtic and world; live studio guests; reads the 'Chicagoland Folk Calendar'. Kuzma joined in April 2001 rotating with the late George Brown and has been sole host since July 2007. (The Woodstock Folk Festival site gives 7-10pm, presumably outdated.)

Thursdays 9-10pm; folk, country, blues and roots-rock from the 1950s-90s. WDCB also carries American Routes (Thu 7-9pm) and several blues shows (Blacks & Blues, Blues Before Sunrise, Blues from the Red Rooster Lounge, Hambone's Blues Party).
Reported Sundays 10am-noon; currency not confirmed (low confidence).
The 8am-midnight schedule grid (fall 2026) shows no dedicated folk, bluegrass or Celtic show, though the station lists 'Folk' as a genre; 'Voices of the Mexican Song' and world-music slots exist.

radio.station: Old Town School of Folk Music (SoundCloud)
radio.notes: Podcast episodes, including an extra episode (14.5) with Ted and Marcia Johnson; series name and currency not verified.

radio.show: Chicago Irish Radio - The O'Connor Show
radio.host: O'Connor family (originally The Mike O'Connor Show)
radio.notes: Saturdays 11am-1pm; 'live on the radio continuously since 1971', now in its third generation of listeners; Irish community news and music. Station call letters not verified (listed as 1490 AM).
Sundays noon-1pm plus a weekly podcast; ties Irish culture and current events to music (trad and contemporary Irish acts).

shops_makers.name: Old Town School Music Store
shops_makers.kind: acoustic and folk instrument shop, rentals, repairs
shops_makers.notes: At 4544 N Lincoln; instrument rentals reservable online, with part of the rental fee applicable to a purchase; repairs. The 2025 audit's 'Sales' line (store and café) was $1.77M.

shops_makers.name: Chicago Music Exchange
shops_makers.notes: 3316 N Lincoln Ave (Roscoe Village); museum-like vintage showroom. Its owner launched Reverb.com in 2013 (sold to Etsy in 2019). Founded 1990 or 1991 (sources differ).

shops_makers.name: Kenneth Warren & Son, Ltd.
shops_makers.notes: In the Loop since 1926 (40 N Wells St); fourth generation (James Warren); founded the Chicago School of Violin Making in 1975.

shops_makers.name: Carl Becker & Son
shops_makers.notes: Family violin-making line going back to Herman Macklett, whose shop burned in the 1871 Great Chicago Fire. Carl G. Becker (1887-1975) worked for Lyon & Healy and William Lewis & Son; with son Carl F. Becker (1919-2013) he made violins from 1948 and opened Carl Becker & Son in 1968. Now run by Paul Becker; 410 S Michigan Ave.

shops_makers.name: Bein & Fushi
shops_makers.notes: Founded by Robert Bein and Geoffrey Fushi; owner and executive director now Gabriel Ben-Dashan; associated with the Stradivari Society. Founding year not verified here.

shops_makers.name: Lyon & Healy
shops_makers.kind: historic instrument maker (harps; formerly guitars, mandolins, banjos)
shops_makers.notes: Founded 1864 as a sheet-music shop; by 1900 made harps, pianos, guitars, mandolins, banjos and ukuleles. Still builds concert and lever (folk) harps at its Chicago headquarters, which has a showroom and concert hall; now a subsidiary of Salvi Harps.

shops_makers.name: Washburn
shops_makers.notes: Established 1883 in Chicago (Lyon & Healy's fretted-instrument brand); the name is now owned by U.S. Music Corp. / Exertis JAM.

shops_makers.name: Harmony Company
shops_makers.notes: Founded 1892 by Wilhelm Schultz; bought by Sears in 1916 (Silvertone); also made Stella, Vogue, Valencia and others; in its heyday the largest US instrument maker, mass-producing about ten million guitars in Chicago between 1945 and 1975; closed 1975 (brand revived by BandLab in 2018).

shops_makers.name: Kay Musical Instrument Company
shops_makers.kind: historic guitar, banjo and mandolin maker
shops_makers.notes: Formed 1931 from Stromberg-Voisinet, whose 1928 'Stromberg Electro' may have been the first commercial electric guitar; sold to Seeburg in 1965 and Valco in 1967; brand later used on imports.

shops_makers.name: Front Porch Music
shops_makers.kind: acoustic music shop with lessons, repairs and open stage
shops_makers.notes: Valparaiso, IN (Porter County), since 1991; 'a picker's paradise'.

shops_makers.name: Fretboard Summit luthier showcase
shops_makers.notes: 94 luthiers and vendors at the Old Town School in August 2025, the most visible annual gathering of independent builders in the metro.

shops_makers.name: Specimen Products / Chicago School of Guitar Making (Ian Schneller)
shops_makers.kind: luthier: handmade guitars, ukuleles, horn speakers and tube amps; building classes
shops_makers.notes: Industrial-corridor workshop known for sculptural instruments; site active May 2025.

shops_makers.name: Geoff Benge's Guitar Shop
shops_makers.notes: 30+ years repairing guitars, mandolins, banjos, resonators and folk instruments including oud, Greek and Irish bouzouki, bajo sexto, Cuban tres, berimbau, hurdy-gurdy, charango, tiple and cuatro, which shows how many diaspora instruments pass through Chicago repair benches.

archives.notes: Launched 2026; polka history, inductees, interview series (video and articles).

archives.name: Library of Congress, American Folklife Center: Chicago Ethnic Arts Project (AFC 1981/004)
archives.notes: 1977 survey with the Illinois Arts Council: 14 folklorists, 26 ethnic groups, ~344 tapes, ~14,000 photos, online since 2016. Includes the Midwest Fleadh at Bogan High School, Terry Teahan, Frank Thornton on the Irish Musicians' Association, Pat Roche and Peggy Roche Boyle on Irish dance, Alabama-born fiddler Nancy Buckalew in Cicero, and Hardanger fiddler Jørgen Hyland in Evanston.

archives.name: Library of Congress: Alan Lomax 1938 Chicago recordings (AFC 1939/007)
archives.notes: Oct 25, 1938 discs recorded in Chicago, e.g. Mrs. Hulan singing with kantele, part of Lomax's Great Lakes collection.

archives.name: Chicago Public Library, Harold Washington Library Center Music Information Center: University of Chicago Folk Festival Collection
archives.notes: 1961-1995, 12 linear feet; 125 of 305 hours of WFMT-recorded festival tapes digitized (Professor Longhair, Sippie Wallace, Bill Monroe, Odetta, the Beers Family).

archives.name: Hyde Park Historical Society: UChicago Folk Fest History Project
archives.notes: Digitized posters, schedules (1969-1982), Maroon articles and oral histories; includes a 1982 old-time music convention poster.

archives.name: University of Chicago Library exhibit 'Putting the Folk Back in Folk Music: Sixty Years of the University of Chicago Folk Festival'
archives.notes: Library exhibit page (bot-gated during research); UChicago Special Collections finding aids are the route to Folklore Society records.

archives.name: Old Town School of Folk Music archive and Resource Center
archives.notes: Resource Center created in the 1987 Armitage renovation; the online history draws on archival photos, audio and Dawn Greening's daily log.

archives.name: WFMT Studs Terkel Radio Archive
archives.notes: 5,000+ conversations over 45 years, many with folk and blues musicians.

archives.name: Digital Chicago: 'Preserving Irish Traditional Music in Chicago: Francis O'Neill'
archives.notes: Online exhibit with O'Neill artifacts from great-granddaughter Mary Lesch, biographies of his sources, maps, and recordings of Liz Carroll, Seán Cleland, Kevin Henry and John Williams.

archives.name: University of Notre Dame, Hesburgh Libraries: O'Neill Collection of Traditional Irish Music and Captain Francis O'Neill Papers
archives.notes: O'Neill's library ('Hiberniana') given in 1931; annotated Bunting and Petrie volumes; correspondence 1931-33. Outside the MSA (South Bend, IN).

archives.name: Ward Irish Music Archives (Milwaukee Irish Fest)
archives.notes: Remastered the O'Neill wax cylinders (c.1904: Cronin, McFadden and others) after they were found in Milwaukee. Outside the MSA.

archives.name: Columbia College Chicago: Center for Black Music Research
archives.notes: Founded 1983; collections on Black music worldwide; closed June 2023-Jan 2024 for renovation, then reopened by appointment.

archives.name: DrDosido's Fiddlers Reunion (Paul Tyler)
archives.notes: Online archive of field recordings and 78s by Chicago fiddlers from 1904 to 2022: Irish, Barn Dance, Polish, tamburitza, Scandinavian, Mexican son, Greek, old-time, and the Adler House and Folk & Roots series.

archives.name: Irish American Heritage Center library, archives and museum
archives.notes: In the former Mayfair School; houses the Irish American Hall of Fame.

archives.name: The Hayloft Gang (film and University of Illinois Press book)
archives.notes: Documentary and essay collection on the National Barn Dance; Paul Tyler was music supervisor and wrote the lead essay 'The Rise of Rural Rhythm'.

archives.name: Old Town School of Folk Music Resource Center
archives.notes: In the basement of the Lincoln Ave campus; over 25,000 commercial and archival recordings, videos, books, photos, documents and periodicals; also an online six-chapter school history with audio clips.

archives.name: WFMT Folkstage archive
archives.notes: About 45 years of archival live folk concerts, some from the Old Town School, rebroadcast on Folkstage; Midnight Special playlists archived online.

archives.name: Library of Congress, American Folklife Center: interview with Noel Rice (1977)
archives.notes: 'Interview with Noel Rice about teaching Irish music and dance in Chicago, Illinois', May 5, 1977 (afc1981004), apparently from the Chicago Ethnic Arts Project.

heritage_traditions.evidence: Two dedicated schools with graded curricula: AfriCaribe (since 2000, Fall 2025 academy) and La Escuelita Bombera de Corazón (since 2009; all seven 2026-27 classes sold out); free bombazos every few months (latest Sep 2026); Muntu's weekly class includes bomba; SRBCC youth percussion apprenticeships; bomba stages at Puerto Rican Fest and Fiesta Boricua.

Los Pleneros de Don Segundo (SRBCC, since 2016) perform original plena; La Escuelita teaches güiro y pandereta plena and runs 'Bombazo y Plenazo' (Nov 2025); AfriCaribe teaches plena dance and drumming.

Jarochicanos collective (since 2008) runs talleres and has organized fandangos for a decade; 18th Street Casa de Cultura programs; Old Town School workshops with Veracruz masters. No dated 2025-26 fandango calendar found; freshest evidence is May 2024.

heritage_traditions.tradition: Mexican regional son (huasteco, gustos, chilenas, jarocho)
heritage_traditions.evidence: Sones de México Ensemble (Pilsen, 1994); its founders became 2026 NEA National Heritage Fellows; school and outreach programs continue.

School-based pipeline: Orozco after-school program 2025-26, Chicago Mariachi Project in CPS, Mariachi Matters (Romeoville, since 2011), UIC Mariachi Festival for high school and community groups (Oct 2025).
Ballet Folklórico de Chicago reports 400+ students, open 7 days; MFDC (1982) rehearses 3x/week; many parish and school groups.
groups: Mexican Folkloric Dance Company of Chicago

heritage_traditions.evidence: Commercial jaripeos and bailes advertised on Eventbrite and social media (Cicero, North Chicago); no stable venue calendar verified. Probably larger than any other heritage dance scene by attendance, but poorly documented.
73rd annual Chicago Powwow Oct 3 2026; Powwow at the Lake started 2024 (500+); AIC weekly Drum & Dance (status after 2023 unverified); Harvest Pow Wow cancelled in 2026.

heritage_traditions.community: Polish, from Podhale (Southwest Side, Archer Ave, Burbank)
heritage_traditions.evidence: ZPPA (1929) calendar full through 2026: Józefinki Muzykanckie, a Podhale soloists' and musicians' review named for Karol Stoch Waka, a dance-pair contest (Oct 18 2026), 43rd Festiwal na Góralską Nutę (Nov 2026); Siumni (2002) plus children's groups.
groups: Polish Highlanders Alliance of North America (ZPPA)

heritage_traditions.tradition: Polish national and regional folk song and dance
heritage_traditions.evidence: Polonia Ensemble weekly classes at Copernicus Center (25+ years); Taste of Polonia since 1979.

heritage_traditions.community: Polish American (now largely 3rd-4th generation, South and Southwest suburbs, NW Indiana)
heritage_traditions.evidence: The IPA's Chicago Festival of Bands continues (58th in Jan 2027), and bands like Lenny Gomulka & Chicago Push and Tony Blazonczyk's New Phaze still play, but the IPA's national convention moves to Erie, PA in 2027 and the IPA calendar lists few Chicago-area dances (one Merrillville, IN event in Nov 2026). Weekly polka dances in Chicago were not verified.

Hromovytsia (1980) active under founder Roxana Dykyj-Pylypczak and her daughter; Chicago Bandura Ensemble concert with the Elgin Symphony (Feb 2025); Ukrainian National Museum workshops. Bandura activity looks niche.
Grandis (1953) six age groups weekly; Spindulys (3 age groups); Suktinis (2005); women's group Vaivora; annual Grandis concert at the Lithuanian World Center.

heritage_traditions.tradition: Tamburitza (Croatian and Serbian string bands) and kolo
heritage_traditions.community: South Slavic (Croatian, Serbian), Chicago and NW Indiana Calumet region
heritage_traditions.evidence: Five Chicago orchestras and Dunav (Schererville, IN) listed for the 2025 TAA Extravaganza; SerbFest Merrillville 2026; junior tamburitzan groups reported. Deep roots: NEA Fellows Adam Popovich (1982) and Milan Opacich (2004).
Embodied by NEA Fellow Nicolae Feraru (2013); no current ensemble or class verified.
Maxwell Street Klezmer Band (1983) monthly Klezmer Night (Nov 2026); Klezmer Music Foundation (1994) runs the Junior Klezmer Orchestra (continuous since 1994) and congregational klezmer bands.

heritage_traditions.tradition: Irish step dance and Irish community culture
heritage_traditions.evidence: Trinity Irish Dance (1982) at nine locations; IAHC (5,000+ members reported) and Chicago Gaelic Park run weekly set dancing, sessions, language classes, the Chicago Feis and Irish Fest (Aug 2026). Chicago produced NEA Fellows Joe Shannon, Michael Flatley and Liz Carroll.
Ensemble Español (1975) professional and youth companies, classes, annual festival; flamenco tablao Oct 2026.
Annual Akitu (Assyrian New Year) parade on Western Ave and parties with khigga; Assyrian dance at the Skokie Festival of Cultures (May 2025). Evidence comes from event aggregators.
groups: Assyrian American Civic Club of Chicago

heritage_traditions.evidence: Parish dance troupes reported at Greek Orthodox churches (Annunciation, St. Demetrios, St. Andrew, Holy Trinity) per search summary; parish festivals. Not independently verified.
KUD Bosna Chicago folklore society and BHACC exist; no dated 2025-26 event found.
KCCoC Chicago Poongmul School (Wheeling); HANA Center adult group IlGwaNoRi (open house June 2025) and women's group Woori Sori; pungmul used in organizing.
Chinese Music Society of North America (reportedly 1976); Chicago Chinese Cultural Institute concerts; UChicago Jade ensemble (2022); erhu recital at World Music Foundation (Sep 2025).
groups: Chinese Music Society of North America

heritage_traditions.evidence: No standing rondalla found. Folk dance is taught by groups such as the Filipino-American Youth Dance Group at Holy Child Jesus parish; Rizal Center events during Filipino American History Month.
groups: Filipino-American Youth Dance Group (Holy Child Jesus)
Filipino American Council of Greater Chicago / Rizal Center

heritage_traditions.evidence: Natya Dance Theatre (1975, 50 years in 2025); Kalapriya's adult and children's classes and Diwali 2026; many smaller schools.

heritage_traditions.tradition: Cambodian pinpeat music and classical dance
heritage_traditions.evidence: The museum's 2026-27 class schedule covers pinpeat, Khmer traditional music and Khmer dance; annual fundraiser Oct 10 2026 with generations of performers.
groups: National Cambodian Heritage Museum & Killing Fields Memorial

heritage_traditions.tradition: West African and African diaspora dance and drum
heritage_traditions.community: African American and African immigrant (South Side)
heritage_traditions.evidence: Muntu Dance Theatre (1972) weekly community class and Oct 2026 auditions; African Festival of the Arts' Drum Village (35th edition 2025).
The Ethiopian Community Association of Chicago is active as a service organization; no Ethiopian music or dance ensemble, class or recurring event found.

heritage_traditions.tradition: Chicago blues as a community practice
heritage_traditions.community: African American (South and West Sides) and blues fans citywide
heritage_traditions.evidence: Weekly ticketed jam at Buddy Guy's Legends (Nov 2026); free monthly Logan Center jam (since Oct 2025); Rosa's jam; suburban jams (Low-reen's list); Chicago Blues Festival since 1984. The neighborhood juke-joint circuit that produced NEA Fellows Sunnyland Slim, Honeyboy Edwards and Koko Taylor has largely thinned out.

heritage_traditions.community: African American (Bronzeville, South and West Sides)
heritage_traditions.evidence: Chicago Gospel Music Festival since 1985 (Jul 24-25 2026); church-based practice embodied by NEA Fellows Albertina Walker (West Point Missionary Baptist Church member 70+ years), Pops and Mavis Staples. Congregational activity is not tallied here.
NEA Fellows Reggio 'the Hoofer' McLaughlin (2021) and Bril Barrett (2024, Bronzeville), who teaches tap with its history in every class.

heritage_traditions.tradition: Southern and Appalachian migrant music (Uptown 'Hillbilly Heaven')
heritage_traditions.evidence: Uptown housed Appalachian and Southern migrants in the 1950s-60s and was nicknamed 'Hillbilly Heaven'; the Council of the Southern Mountains opened the Chicago Southern Center there in 1963. No living successor scene found.

heritage_traditions.tradition: Swedish, Norwegian and Czech folk music and dance
heritage_traditions.evidence: Swedish American Museum (founded 1976) programs language, crafts and holidays, but no folk-music ensemble or dance found in this pass. Czech and Norwegian community music not found. Scandinavian dance is covered by the trad-dance thread.

Free city-run Chicago Gospel Music Festival (2026: July 24-25, community choir showcase plus national headliners); Thomas A. Dorsey co-founded the National Convention of Gospel Choirs and Choruses in Chicago in 1932. Quartet-anniversary culture was not separately documented in this research. Chorus America (2018) says the 'churchy style of Dorsey and Frye is alive in Chicago' through traditional gospel choirs whose history runs through Ebenezer and Pilgrim Baptist churches.

people.name: Adam Popovich
people.notes: Living in Dolton, IL at the time of the award. With brothers Eli and Ted formed the Popovich Brothers tamburitza orchestra (1925), most popular in the Indiana steel towns and Chicago; steel-mill millwright; directed the Sloboda choir at St. Archangel Michael Serbian Orthodox Church after 1936. In the first class of Fellows.
